newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares slow down after bullish trend.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares slow down after bullish trend.

text.p: Many leading Russian shares ended off early highs on Thursday, and some closed the day with net losses.
A rally which set in late Wednesday on news doctors believe they can operate successfully on President Boris Yeltsin faded, dealers said, adding they expected a quiet Friday.
The 24-company index of the Russian Trading System rose on Thursday by 2.84 percent to 164.24 on $11.94 million in volume -- about half the volume of the last two days.

"There was pretty big buying late on Wednesday. It was pretty bullish this morning, but this buying subsided by the afternoon, as no additional news on Yeltsin has come out," said Nick Mokhoff of Alliance-Menatep.
A council of surgeons including one American announced on Wednesday afternoon after examining Yeltsin that he could be successfully operated on in six or eight weeks.
"The news which came out yesterday was first of all very well perceived in the West, because Yeltsin had an American doctor, who has given his health analysis," Mokhoff said.

"Shares continued to grow in the morning, because big Western buying orders that appeared on the good Yeltsin news late on Wednesday had to be completed... Then prices steadied," said Andrei Ippolitov of Prospekt.
He said some shares had been overbought on Wednesday and were now being corrected.

LUKoil, which said it was opening a huge filling station in Belarus, rose to $9.05 from $8.95 at Wednesday's close, but ended off its early $9.30 high. UES rose to $0.0730 from $0.0715, ending off a $0.0749 high, and Mosenergo edged up to $0.865 from $0.850, after a $0.895 high.
Ippolitov said he expected most shares would be little changed on Friday, especially if no major news arrives.
"The market could either fall or rise, but very slightly, by one or two percent," Ippolitov said.
Mokhoff said the market could stagnate over the two months before Yeltsin's operation.
